articleTitle: Techno-economic and environmental analysis of Amity University Noida rooftop SPV generation: Towards a Net zero future
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Solar power is more powerful than most people realize and is the most abundant source of energy. By utilizing solar PV panels, which transform sunlight into electrical energy, we can harness the power of the sun. To meet the educational campus’ energy needs, an on-grid solar photovoltaic (SPV) plant is assessed and examined in this study. Alongside extensive economic and environmental assessments are provided, together with detailed financial and technical statistics pertaining to system aspects. PVsyst is used to help the system’s technical evaluation, economic analysis, and design. The analysis’s conclusions led to the conclusion that the PV installation is expected to produce 100 KWh of energy. The system shows a performance ratio of 81.51%, with a total efficiency of 15.3%.

articleTitle: Three Phase Reduced Switch Count 19 level Inverter using a Three Phase Two level Inverter and four Single Phase H Bridges
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: A three-phase 19-level inverter topology is presented in this paper. The presented topology uses four single-phase H-bridges (HB) and a three-phase two-level inverter (TLI). This reduced switch topology utilizes 22 switches for its voltage level generation which is low compared to many other topologies. The nearest level modulation (NLM) technique is used for the voltage level generation. MATLAB simulation is done for the proposed scheme and a comparative table with other topologies is also shown.

articleTitle: Speed Control of Switched Reluctance Motor Using Double Switch Quasi-Z Source High-Gain DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative SRM drive system that incorporates a Double Switch Quasi-Z-Source (DSQZS) high-gain DC-DC converter to boost energy efficiency and enhance performance. The system is powered primarily by a 12V battery in combination with the DSQZS converter, which elevates the DC-link voltage required for optimal motor function, particularly under fluctuating loads and transient states. A secondary high-voltage battery is integrated to extend the operational range, with the smaller battery recharging the larger one when the motor is inactive. This configuration helps alleviate range anxiety and optimizes energy transfer within the drive system. A hysteresis controller manages the switching pulses, ensuring stable and efficient operation. The proposed system enhances both control precision and stability, while minimizing energy loss, making it suitable for high-performance motor applications. To regulate the speed of the SRM, a PI controller is used due to its simplicity and effectiveness across various control scenarios. This integrated approach addresses typical SRM challenges, such as torque ripple and nonlinear behavior, while ensuring accurate speed control. Simulations carried out in MATLAB/Simulink confirm that the system achieves stable speed regulation and significantly reduces torque ripple. The findings underline the potential of the proposed method to improve dynamic performance and reliability, making it well-suited for industrial settings where both efficiency and compact design are essential.

articleTitle: IoT Enabled Vehicle Monitoring and Theft Prevention System (I-VMTPS)
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: An IoT enabled vehicle monitoring and theft prevention system is a comprehensive solution that uses Internet of Things (IoT) technology to track and manage vehicles in real-time, enhance security, and reduce the risk of theft. This paper implements the design and implementation of IoT based Vehicle Monitoring and Theft Prevention System (I-VMTPS). The system is divided into two parts: part A is Monitoring and part B is theft prevention system. The reported system integrates existing technology such as GPS and GSM to monitor the vehicle. GPS is used in tracking systems and for SMS based communication GSM is used. GPS and GSM technology working together will provide efficient, real-time vehicle location and log of owner information. Part B is a mechanism that makes vehicle theft almost impossible. Two security features are offered by the described system: a remote ignition cut-off mechanism and vehicle password protection. The sensors are used for accident detection. This system represents a sophisticated and versatile solution that addresses the growing need for vehicle security and management in an increasingly connected world, contributing to safer and more efficient vehicle operations.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis of Domestic Energy Consumption Using Python and Matplotlib
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Inefficient energy consumption is a global issue, with domestic energy usage rising consistently in the Ludhiana district of Punjab, India, due to population growth and lack of awareness about proper energy use, leading to significant waste. This research utilizes Python and Matplotlib to thoroughly examine household energy consumption. It evaluates the financial and environmental benefits of using energy-efficient household equipment. The study estimates daily energy savings, cost savings, and the payback period for the investment in new appliances. With an anticipated payback period of 1.77 years, the results show substantial savings in energy usage and expenses. The report highlights environmental advantages such as reduced greenhouse gas emissions. By promoting the adoption of energy-efficient devices, this research aims to educate consumers and support regulatory initiatives to enhance sustainability.By replacing old devices, substantial reductions in greenhouse gas emissions (4838 $\mathrm{kg} \mathrm{CO} 2 / \mathrm{year}$) and electricity costs are achieved.

articleTitle: Real-Time Brain Signals Monitoring System Using Single-Channel EEG for BCI Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: This study presents the development of a system for real-time monitoring of brain signals using a wearable device equipped with a single-channel EEG sensor. Brain signals, acquired through a custom-designed data acquisition protocol, are used to monitor cognitive and physiological states during various events. The labeled data are utilized to train a deep learning model. EEG signals are processed using a microcontroller and visualized using a graphical user interface (GUI). Data collection from participants was conducted under three different conditions: eyes open, eyes closed, and motor imagery tasks involving hand opening and closing. These conditions serve as training inputs for a deep learning model, enabling it to learn and classify signal patterns associated with different events. The acquired signals are analyzed by extracting various features and visualizing time-frequency domain properties for class differentiation. This system holds potential applications in cognitive and physiological monitoring and applications in brain-computer interface (BCI), such as prosthetic arm control, with the added benefits of low-power, cost-effective edge computing and green computing for sustainable deployment.

articleTitle: Battery State of Health Prognostic based on Neural Hierarchical Interpolation
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: The precise State of Health (SOH) estimation of Lithium-ion Batteries (LIB) is critical for analyzing the dependability and endurance of battery-powered systems. SOH estimate using data driven techniques has gained popularity in recent years. The approach envisions the possibility to harness battery information and also supports in cloud-based battery management techniques. In this proposed work, novel data driven SOH estimation approach was carried out and performance metrics including RMSE, MAPE, and coefficient of determination (R-square) were calculated, to evaluate the efficacy of the proposed approach. To build and validate the model, experimental data of LIB were taken from NASA website. The performance metrics of the proposed model is compared against similar deep learning and machine learning models to analyze the improvisation of accuracy. The proposed Linear-NHI model achieves the lowest error inclusive of RMSE as 0.004, MAPE as $\mathbf{0. 4 9 \%}$ and attains highest coefficient of determination as $\mathbf{9 5 \%}$ for $\mathbf{B 0 0 0 5}$ model. For B0018 model, the performance metrics are similarly evaluated: RMSE, MAPE and $R^{2}$ are obtained as $\mathbf{0. 0 0 6 5}, \mathbf{0. 7 5 5}$ and $\mathbf{7 7. 6 \%}$ respectively thereby securing improved accuracy and reliability in SOH estimation. The findings emphasise the potential of advanced modelling techniques and is helpful to improve the operational efficiency and maintenance of Lithium-ion battery.

articleTitle: Advanced IoT Enabled Irrigation and Seed Sowing System with Dual Axis Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: By focusing on technology-driven solutions for agriculture, particularly in seed sowing and water management, addressing crucial challenges is the research focus. A sophisticated agricultural system that combines multiple technologies to optimize farming efficiency is being proposed along with usage of Solar energy. Automating irrigation and utilizing renewable energy sources will not only boost agricultural productivity but also help in minimizing environmental footprints. The integration of an automated seed sowing model is especially intriguing. Automating the planting process can indeed enhance precision and speed, while reducing labour costs. The approach and the model proposed will not only streamline farm operations but also contribute to improved efficiency, water conservation, and energy savings. Overall, the work carried out offers a comprehensive solution for modern farming practices, encompassing automated irrigation, seed sowing, and sustainability measures.

articleTitle: Multi-Role Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: This study investigates various aspects of fixedwing Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), from conceptual design to hardware implementation, focusing on control system development. Key UAV design characteristics and achievable flight modes are discussed. The mathematical model, including force, moment, and orientation equations, is presented. UAV Toolbox from MATLAB was used to develop control systems for stabilization and navigation. Controllers for pitch, yaw, roll, and altitude control loops were designed and tested. Results demonstrate the efficacy of these controllers in ensuring stable and responsive UAV performance across different flight scenarios.

articleTitle: Development of Wireless Inductive Power Transfer Converter with Variable Load
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: This paper demonstrates the sending of power from input side to output side by the method of Wireless Inductive Power Transfer (WIPT). A variable load is used to analyse the efficiency of the device. Also the decrease of induced voltage with the increase in distance between primary and secondary is studied. This technique has a high potential in electric vehicle charging. The power is transferred after converting to high frequency through a HF converter circuit. The efficiency highly depends on the converter circuit. With the increase in load the efficiency is increased till optimal level. With the increase in load, the developed voltage will be reduced till certain level after which there is no induced potential in secondary coil.

articleTitle: Comparison of Tree Based Model Feature Importances With SHAP Scores
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Heart failure, which affects over 64 million individuals globally, is a serious health problem. Early and accurate prediction is crucial for reducing its impact. Researchers have employed various machine learning models to address this challenge. Our aim is to find whether the importance scores generated by random forest, gradient boost, and XGBoost agree with the explain-ability method. This paper shows the prediction model whose feature importances agree with the Shapley values for our selected dataset. We also compare feature importance scores of three prediction algorithms random forest, gradient boost, and XGBoost with SHAP (Shapley Additive exPlanations) to find their agreement on scores. We use the UCI “Heart Failure Clinical Records” collection from the UCI Machine Learning Repository, which has $\mathbf{2 9 9}$ patients in its heart failure dataset.

articleTitle: Design, Control, Operation and Stability of Grid-connected DC Microgrid with Constant Power Load
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: The paper investigates the design, control, operation, and stability of grid-connected DC microgrids. A DC microgrid consists of PV generation, a Li-ion battery for high-energy density storage, a supercapacitor for high-power density storage, an electric vehicle load, and a constant power load (CPL). A three-level neutral-point clamped (NPC) converter facilitates the interface between the utility AC grid and the DC microgrid. A DC-DC boost converter and two DC-DC bidirectional converters respectively connect the PV array, battery, and supercapacitor to the common DC bus. Battery and supercapacitor are coordinated to operate as a composite energy storage system (CESS). In this, batteries supply DC and low-frequency components of load power, whereas supercapacitors supply transient and high-frequency components. DC-DC upper stream converters feed to electronically controlled load, which behaves as CPL and causes instantaneous instability. The proposed CESS scheme performs three functions simultaneously, viz., energy-time shift, proper load sharing among various resources, and active stabilizer. This scheme improves power quality at the DC side as well as the AC side continuously against both AC side fault and DC side disturbance caused by source and load. In addition, it works as active stabilization to mitigate the instability caused by constant power load. A single controller for these two bidirectional converters is designed and developed to serve the specified functions. In this research, a suitable grid-connected DC microgrid is designed, and AC side faults, DC side disturbances, and instability due to CPL with their mitigations are simulated and verified. The proposed scheme is simulated in MATLAB Simulink software, and the results are validated with OPAL-RT (RT-4510) based Hardware In Loop (HIL) real-time simulator.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulating PMSG based Wind Turbines using a Fuzzy Logic Controlled DC-Link Protection Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: The electricity produced by wind turbines with PMSGs (permanent magnet synchronous generators) is typically sent to the grid using a device known as a back-to-back converter. Faults within the transmission system can cause power imbalances between the converters, leading into a considerable rise in the DC-link voltage. This voltage surge poses a risk of damaging the system of converters and negatively impacting the system’s overall temporary stability. Several methods have been proposed to control the overvoltage in the DC-link, including the installation of unloading circuits or to absorb extra power, devices for energy storage are added to the DC-link bus. However, these approaches necessitate additional equipment, increasing system costs and complicating the control strategy. In conventional systems, a DC chopper and a braking resistor are typically employed across the DC-link to guarantee the stability of active power. These protection mechanisms are not effective in managing the dissipated power in a productive manner. This study suggests a fuzzy logic-controller for the DC-link circuit in order to solve this problem. To manage overvoltage in the DC-link and stabilize the output power of PMSG-based wind energy systems, a DC-link voltage control technique based on fuzzy logic is presented. Simulations of the PMSG-based wind energy system confirm that this fuzzy logic control approach is effective.

articleTitle: Comparing various workflow scheduling algorithms based on cost-time tradeoff criteria for clouds
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Cloud scheduling of workflow applications have become a great challenge, especially when we are dealing with many QoS (Quality of Service) constraints. Scheduling Workflow tasks onto instances of VMs in heterogeneous cloud environments have become challenging. Many cloud scheduling algorithms based on multi-objective QoS constraints. We have compared cloud scheduling algorithms justifying cost-time trade of criteria in our research. Our work emphasizes on both static and dynamic cloud scheduling algorithm for clouds. We have compared these under various parameters and conditions such as research gaps or drawbacks of the proposed algorithm, trade-off function used, task selection strategy used and many more.

articleTitle: Role of FACTS Devices Incorporating Renewable Energy Sources in Distribution and Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: The imperative to incorporate renewable energy sources into distribution systems is magnifying, pressurizing grid infrastructure to accept the inherent stochasticity of renewable generation. In this survey, investigation is done for the pivotal contribution of FACTS in expressing the embodiment of RES into transmission and distribution system. With the global recognition and usage of RE, distribution network and transmission face some defiance with respect to regulation of voltage, power reliability management, and grid stability. To address these concerns FACTS devices assists dynamic control capabilities consequently facilitating the consistent enactment of renewable energy into distribution grids. With an elaborative inclusion of existing literature and empirical studies, this paper elucidates the various operational mechanisms, control methodologies, and study of deployment strategies of all categories of FACTS devices, such as Static VAR Compensators, UPFC and Static Synchronous Compensators. By mentioning future research directions this paper aimed at harnessing the full potential of FACTS devices in facilitating the transition towards sustainable and resilient distribution and transmission systems powered by renewable energy sources.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency and Sustainability Initiatives in the Semiconductor Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Semiconductor industry is foundational to the digital age as it drives the production of essential electronic devices. However, it faces the challenge of substantial electricity consumption. This paper investigates the energy footprint of semiconductor manufacturing processes. Previous studies indicate that semiconductor fabrication units (fabs) have significant electricity consumption and often rely on nonrenewable energy sources. Many of the advanced processes in its manufacturing require higher energy inputs, where clean-room maintenance and material usage contribute significantly to consumption. Despite many efforts, electricity usage trends show an upward trajectory, indicating growing operations and technological advancements. This research analyzes the energy distribution within the fab as well as discusses the measures that can improve the consumption patterns. We discuss how the measures that can be taken for balancing growth with sustainability. Addressing the challenge requires investments in research for renewable energy adoption, and smart energy management systems. Innovations in equipment, cooling systems, and recycling practices are some of the avenues for reducing energy consumption. Therefore, urgent action is important to minimize this industry’s environmental impact while meeting the rising demand for semiconductor products. This demands innovation for achieving sustainability goals in the semiconductor industry.

articleTitle: Advanced Microstrip Patch Antenna Sensor Design for Salt and SugarDetection in Liquids to Support Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: To prevent many health diseases it is very essential that salt and sugar content should be consumed in appropriate amount in the food items. This study presents the design and advancement of a microstrip patch antenna for distinguishing saltiness and sugar levels. The proposed antenna works at 1.33 GHz that is powered by a microstrip line. Simulation and optimization of designed antenna are performed by using the High-Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS). The performance of proposed antenna sensor is tested in solution with different salt and sugar concentrations. The measurement of reflection coefficient of simulated microstrip patch antenna sensor are performed with sugar and salt concentrations in a solution. From the experimental results it is found that the reflection coefficient decreases as the sugar and salt level increases in the solution. The proposed microstrip patch antenna offers a lightweight and cost-effective device for sugar and salt identification in any solution.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis of Simultaneous Integration of Optimal DG And D-STATCOM Allocation In Distribution System With Intermittent Nature of Load
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: This study focuses on optimizing the placement and sizing of Distribution Static Compensators (D-STATCOMs) and Distributed Generations (DGen) in a radial distribution network (RN) to minimize power losses and enhance voltage profiles (VP). Using the Voltage Stability Index (VSI) and Loss Sensitivity Factor (LSF), two scenarios were analyzed: (Case I) D-STATCOMs and DGen at the same site and (Case II) at separate locations, across normal, light, and peak loading conditions. Utilizing the Forward Backward Sweep (FBS) method and Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) on an IEEE 33bus system, results indicated that Case II resulted in significant reductions of real power losses: ${7 5. 5 7 \%}$, ${7 6. 3 0 \%}$, and ${7 5. 6 6 \%}$, respectively, outperforming Case I’s reductions of ${7 0. 3 5 \%}$, ${7 2. 1 8 \%}$, and 71.32%. Additionally, reactive power losses were reduced more effectively in Case II. Although the combined arrangement slightly enhanced voltage profiles more, distinct placements proved more effective overall in optimizing distribution system performance.

articleTitle: Study on the stability of the blends of biodiesel and diesel treated with antioxidant tert-butyl hydroquinone (TBHQ)
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Diesel engines are essential for agriculture, industry, and transportation; however, their dependence on fossil fuels presents significant challenges. This reliance not only accelerates climate change but also causes environmental degradation. In response, biofuels, particularly biodiesel, have emerged as feasible and ecologically sound alternatives. This study investigates the procedure of producing and enhancing biodiesel by using equal quantities of WCO and WPO. TBHQ (tert-butylhydroquinone), a synthetic antioxidant, is added to the biodiesel to enhance its oxidation resistance. The fuel properties of the biodiesel blends, when combined with regular diesel at volume ratios of $20 \%$ and $40 \%$, were evaluated during a 10 -week period. The factors examined comprised acid value, density, and kinematic viscosity. The findings revealed that TBHQ substantially improved the oxidative stability of pure biodiesel. However, its effectiveness diminished as the biodiesel content in the blend increased. Both storage duration and conditions had a significant impact on oxidative stability, with the induction period falling below the 20 -hour mark after 4 to 6 weeks. While antioxidants notably influenced the acid value, their effect on kinematic viscosity was minimal. This research highlights TBHQ's potential for maintaining biodiesel quality under oxidative stress, offering valuable insights for improving the stability of biodiesel blends during long-term storage and ensuring compliance with strict environmental standards.

articleTitle: Source camera identification for securing AI-enabled surveillance cameras
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: The use of IP-based smart cameras for video surveillance has increased tremendously over the last decade with an estimate of over 1 billion surveillance cameras installed worldwide. The recorded images and videos are used by professionals for crime prevention, traffic management, and other data driven analysis. By launching different types of attacks on the IP cameras, the source images and video footage can be corrupted, which would lead to wrong decision making. In this paper, we have proposed to use source camera identification using a tunable filter bank based feature in a video surveillance system for authenticating the original source of an image or video taken from a smart IP camera. For the feature matching several distance measures are used. With Canberra distance, we have achieved state-of-the-art accuracy using 36 features.

articleTitle: Ensemble learning-based detection of hemiplegia using electromyographic signals
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Hemiplegia is a medical condition that can have a profound impact on an individual’s mobility and gait, frequently stemming from strokes. Physical examination is typically utilized as the primary diagnostic method for this ailment. Although a more thorough evaluation can be attained by utilizing electromyographic signals, precisely capturing muscle activity is difficult due to variability and noise, impairing classification accuracy. This study proposes an ensemble learning approach to overcome these limitations and enhance the accuracy of hemiplegic gait classification. The proposed method leverages the strengths of multiple classifiers to achieve improved classification accuracy. As a comparison, the Random Forest Classifier had the highest accuracy of ${97.34 \%}$, followed by the decision tree at ${96.29 \%}$ and the k-nearest neighbor at ${95.40 \%}$. An ensemble of these three classifiers improved accuracy to 98%, accompanied by impressive Precision of 98%, Recall of ${97 \%}$, F1-Score of ${98 \%}$, and Area Under the Curve score of ${99.70 \%}$. The findings of this study can contribute to the development of more accurate and reliable systems for the classification of hemiplegic gait, which can have a significant impact in various clinical and research settings.

articleTitle: Application of Soft Sets Theory in Electric Mobility: Vehicle-to-Grid, Grid-to-Vehicle, and Charging Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: The increasing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) necessitates advanced integration techniques with the power grid to maximize efficiency and sustainability. This research explores the application of soft sets theory to enhance decision-making processes in Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G), Grid-to-Vehicle (G2V), and charging infrastructure systems. Soft sets theory, known for handling uncertainties and imprecision, offers a robust framework for managing the complex variables involved in electric mobility. This study develops a decision-making model incorporating soft sets to evaluate and optimize various scenarios and strategies in electric mobility. The effectiveness of model is validated through case studies and simulation, demonstrating significant improvements in grid stability, economic feasibility, and user satisfaction. The findings underscore the potential of soft sets theory to address the challenges and leverage the opportunities in the evolving landscape of electric mobility.

articleTitle: Predictive analysis of load at EVCS with deep learning algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: This paper considers Electric vehicle charging station(EVCS) as load and predicts the total charging power demand of an EVCS with deep learning algorithms. For pragmatic approach different categories of electric vehicles like electric bikes, electric scooters, electric cars and electric trucks are considered. Their arrival estimate is compared with non-homogeneous Poisson process and it comes under category of M1/M2/C queuing method. The EVCS load is a function of number of vehicles charging at a time, total charging current for each category at a particular time, arrival rate and time of vehicles. These independent parameters are related to the total charging power demand at an EVCS. Different Neural network(NN) optimization techniques like simple gradient descent, full batch gradient descent, stochastic batch gradient descent, adagrad and adam are used for better model representation of EVCS load which can be used for further analysis.

articleTitle: Stress analysis of EEG signal using K-means clustering and hybrid classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: A significant factor that affects both mental and physical health is stress. Measuring accurately the stress level is very important. In this research, we approach measuring the stress using an EEG signal. There are many techniques to measure this stress; the most common ones are PET, ECG, EMG, and MRI, which help in measuring the stress levels of people. Another technique that is very useful and common, i.e., EEG, is mostly used to do such data analysis. EEG plays a very important role in detecting and correcting brain illness. EEG measures the electrical activity of the brain using small metal electrodes attached to the scalp. This activity results in wave lines of EEG signals. Here, we used a combination of the K-means algorithm and SVM-supervised machine learning algorithm to analyze the EEG data. K-means algorithm is used to divide and attempt to cluster the data while the SVM algorithm is used to classify the stress level based on these clusters. The main objective of this model is to improve the accuracy of stress detection by using the strength of both supervised and unsupervised machine learning algorithms. Using this hybrid approach, we attempt to provide a more precise and reliable method for detecting stress in real-time EEG data, with wide application in biomedical diagnosis, mental health monitoring, and many more.

articleTitle: Optimized Continuous Quality and Storage Management Model for Big Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Due to the increase in devices and the availability of connecting devices, data creation increased gradually. To handle the huge amount of data from many different sources, the business analysis had to use effective analysis and storage optimization. So, one of the main areas of research to handle big data, keep its quality up, and get the most out of storage is how to analyze and store big data. This paper introduced a new framework for collaborative big data analysis and optimized storage using the new framework model. The proposed framework model is D2SAE (Dynamic Domain Sample Attributes Evaluation). The proposed framework comprises four main steps: dynamic data collection from domains, sample attribute collection, evaluation metrics for quality data analytics, and an optimization process. The proposed framework was evaluated using metrics such as throughput, runtime, average latency, minimum latency, and maximum latency. Our proposed model produces better throughput and reduces runtime and latency compared to the previous framework. The results show that the throughput increases and the run time is reduced to 42 seconds.

articleTitle: Exploring Different Bypass Schemes for Photovoltaic Modules in Partial Shading Conditions: A Comprehensive Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) energy stands as a pivotal force in modern society, offering significant potential for reducing our carbon footprint. Despite its widespread adoption, commercial-grade PV modules face various technological challenges, notably hotspots caused by partial shading. Traditionally, a single bypass diode across one-third of module cells addresses this issue, but recent research shows its inadequacy, leading to hotspots and premature failure. In response, recent technological advancements introduce alternative solutions using solid-state switches, showing promising results in enhancing bypass circuits' effectiveness. This study examines two bypass schemes across PV panels of the arrays with different configurations. Results highlight the superiority of employing solid-state switches (Power MOSFET) in the bypass path. This innovative approach surpasses conventional methods, offering a compelling solution to the persistent challenges facing commercial-grade PV modules.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Kidney Disease Prediction Using Machine Learning Classification Algorithms and Ensemble Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is very dangerous disease and also represented by chronic kidney failure. In CKD, continuous loss of kidneys with time and stops functioning after some time. According to various survey report of World Health Organization, growth rate of CKD patients is increasing rapidly worldwide every year. Kidneys are the preliminary source of our body for blood cleaning by removing waste and it is also highly responsible for regulating salt, potassium and $\mathrm{p H}$ levels in the body. It manages production of red blood cells and also regulates blood pressure in the body by producing hormones. The main aim of this research paper to design predictive model for detection of early CKD that helps patients get medical treatment at the right time and helps to reduce the loss of lives. Artificial Intelligence playing a very demanded role in field of health sector f or prediction of disease and uncountable research studies have been conducted for categorizing CKD using various machine learning classification algorithms. The effectiveness of any algorithm depends upon selecting the specific key features, applying the best feature extraction techniques, and productive classifier models. Proposed model, uses the Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) method for feature selections and various classification and ensembles algorithms. The accuracy of ensemble models is better than as compared to machine learning models. The accuracy of KNN model is lowest among all model with score ${0 . 6 9 \%}$ and Random Forest model achieved highest accuracy score with value $0,91 \%$. The accuracy score of ensemble boosting model is found to ${0 . 9 8 \%}$. Various accuracy metrics are applied to measure the performance of proposed models like confusion metrics, F1- score, Precision and Recall etc. Among all applied models, the RF classification algorithm and AdaB ensemble methods have achieved high accuracy and linear regression achieved the lowest accuracy.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Artificial Intelligence based models for the Identification of Uterine Cancer
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Uterine cancer identification is a critical task in medical diagnostics since early detection improves patient health. Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) have both showed promise in this discipline as artificial intelligence has advanced. The present paper offers a thorough analysis and comparison of ML and DL methods for uterine cancer detection. Several algorithms, datasets, and assessment criteria have been evaluated in this study in order to ascertain which method performs best. Graphical presentations and tabular comparisons are used to examine the data and show the advantages and disadvantages of each approach. The results conclude that DL based models perform better than typical ML models in terms of accuracy and predictive power, even if both strategies offer advantages.

articleTitle: Improved Efficiency Of Fog And Cloud Computing Paradigms
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: For effective energy management in smart grids, this research suggests a FOG computing architecture that bridges the gap between the edge and CLOUD. Facing data congestion in both traditional edge and CLOUD computing, the system utilizes a two-tiered approach. By preprocessing and filtering sensor data from buildings, edge nodes reduce latency and network traffic. The FOG layer in turn effectively filters data for potential CLOUD processing while doing real time analysis and decision-making depending on immediate needs. With latency reduction of up to $98.7 \%$, the simulation demonstrates significant benefits over CLOUD only approaches and enables real time energy adjustments that optimize resource utilization. Overall, scalability and efficient data handling overcome CLOUD limitations, while enhanced security minimizes reliance on a central CLOUD. This distributed brain for the grid paves the way for a smarter, more responsive energy landscape, powered by intelligence at the edge.

articleTitle: Effect of Input and Fuzzy Membership Function on ANFIS Controller in DFIG-Based Wind Energy Conversion System
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: This work investigates how input and fuzzy membership functions affect the effectiveness of an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) controller designed for managing active and reactive power in a grid-coupled Doubly Fed Induction Generator Wind Energy Conversion System (DFIG-WEC). The test scheme involves of two interconnected DFIG wind turbines that interface through the grid over a bidirectional converter. To control the Direct link capacitor potential difference in the DFIG generation plant, the ANFIS regulatory framework is applied directly to the Grid Side Converter. The proposed method considers single, double input and various membership functions, such as triangular, trapezoidal, and Gaussian, to examine their effectiveness in the ANFIS controller in power output control in changing situations. In this work, the effect of these different membership functions has been tested under conditions of varying wind speeds and grid failures using extensive simulations in MATLAB/Simulink. These results demonstrate how the membership function selection impacts the controller’s performance. This study emphasises the significance of selecting membership functions suitable for practical settings to guarantee the overall stability and effectiveness of DFIG-WECS. These results are, therefore, very useful in designing and optimizing ANFIS controllers for renewable energy systems, targeting the critical role of membership functions in attaining improved dynamic performance and power grid compatibility. The findings thus set a foundation for further progress in intelligent control strategies for sustainable energy solutions.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis of Soiling on Performance of Photovoltaic using ARIMA and LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Solar panels in outdoor settings are frequently exposed to pollutants like dirt, dust, sediment, and bird droppings, which is results in a reduction of output total power generation by as much as $50 \%$. It is imperative to consider the effect of soiling on panels in order to precisely assess the power output of these systems. This paper proposes time series forecasting to predict power generated in clean and soiled panel. This prediction is done based on the data collected real time for clean and soiled panel. The proposed algorithm used for this purpose is ARIMA and LSTM. A comparison between ARIMA and LSTM is done through various parameters, study shows that LSTM outperform and predict soiling loss accurately as compared to ARIMA, ARIMA provides better computational time.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis of Field Oriented Control Technique for Three-Phase Induction Motor Drive in Electric Vehicles Application
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: The Induction motor (IM) is found to be applicable in electric vehicles (EVs) due to its robustness, reliability, and efficiency. Induction motors in EVs are controlled using variable frequency drives (VFDs) or inverters, which can adjust both the frequency and magnitude of the AC supply delivered to the motor. VFDs are tuned to adjust frequency or V/F ratio to precisely regulate the speed. However, VFDs have high torque ripples, causing noise and vibrations in the motor. These noises and vibrations further enter into the EV frame and hence cause serious disturbances to the rider as well as the vehicle structure. The field-oriented control (FOC) technique decouples the motor’s torque and flux components, allowing independent control and providing precise control over the speed and torque. This paper discusses the application of the field-oriented control for speed regulation of induction motors in EV applications. The MATLAB simulation model is developed, and results are presented to demonstrate speed control. The simulation results are validated by deploying the technique on a hardware model with a 1 HP, $440 \mathrm{~V}, 1500$ RPM, squirrel cage three-phase IM.

articleTitle: Robotic Weed Removal Using Deep Learning for Precision Farming
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: This research explores the integration of intelligent robotics and deep learning for precise weed management in cotton field. Utilizing the YOLOv5 model, the study evaluates real-time weed detection, weed removal efficiency and achieving high accuracy across varied weed types in controlled environments. Key contributions include the development of a delta robot system for automated weed removal and the utilization of the “CottonWeeds” dataset, enabling robust model training. Findings underscore the importance of accurate positional error testing and calibration for effective robotic deployment. The study advocates for sustainable agricultural practices by minimizing herbicide use through targeted weed control strategies. Future research aims to enhance model accuracy and scalability, advancing the field of precision agriculture towards increased crop productivity and environmental sustainability.

articleTitle: Sustainable Production Inventory Model with Green Technology Investment under Carbon Tax and Carbon Cap and Trade policy
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to find the optimal decision for manufacturers with low carbon inventory management and also to optimize the total cost for the manufacturer. Carbon emission has become a crucial problem. To reduce carbon emissions, we applied green technology investment and different carbon regulation policies. In this paper, an EPQ model with a demand-dependent production rate that functions of investment in green technology and promotion is developed with different carbon regulations policies. In this study, we optimize the total cost. The numerical example is carried out to find the numerical value of the total cost and sensitivity analysis is carried out to find the significant effects of different carbon regulations on the total cost. From the sensitivity analysis, it is revealed that the carbon tax system has greater benefits than cap-and-trade and limits carbon regulations to minimize the manufacturer’s total cost. This model is developed for the economic production quantity model with different carbon emission regulation policies.

articleTitle: Mitigation of Nonlinearity in Grid Current By D-STATCOM
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: A grid-connected Distribution Static Synchronous Compensator (D STATCOM) with a control algorithm based on Instantaneous Reactive Power Theory (IRPT) is designed and implemented in this study to address power quality problems when nonlinear loads are present. As increases nonlinearity in power system the grid current become more distorted. Nonlinearity in load effect grid current wave shape and this effect is minimize by using D-STATCOM. This article focus on the mitigation of grid current related power quality isuue and harmonic current regulation is made achievable using the Instantaneous Reactive Power Theory (IRPT) control algorithm. The instantaneous active and reactive power components are computed using the IRPT control algorithm, which makes it possible to precisely generate compensating currents to offset the distortions brought on by nonlinear loads. By ensuring that the grid only provides the essential active power component, this method enhances power quality. Voltage source converters (VSCs) which operate as DSTATCOMs use a proportional-integral (PI) controller that keeps the voltage at the DC-link constant.

articleTitle: Advancing Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) Diagnosis: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a non-communicable disease in which our kidneys are stop functioning with time. Accordingly, World Health Organization survey reports, during year 1990 to 2023, life loss caused by CKD were increased up to $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$. The growth rate of CKD patients also increasing rapidly and presently 850 million people across world are suffering from CKD. The kidneys are preliminary requirements for well running of our body and its cleans all waste from the blood. It also controls the red blood cells’ production and regulates the blood pressure in the body by producing hormone. The stage5 is most dangerous stage of CKD. Sometime, very difficult to manage the complication of CKD and treatment of CKD is also very costly. The early detection of CKD is very helpful for minimizing economic burden on patients and as well as, very effective for making appropriate treatment well in advance. In this work, machine learning and deep learning classification models are used for early prediction of CKD. The size of dataset contain 400 CKD patients records with 24 clinical parameters. The classification models such as Logistic Regression (LR), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and MLP with backpropagation, are used to for prediction of CKD. Accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score evaluation for each model were performed using $\mathbf{1 0}$-fold cross-validation. The backpropagation model received highest accuracy score value with 86.5 % among all classification models and logistic regression has received lowest accuracy with 74.2%.

articleTitle: Synergistic Benefits of LVRT and DSTATCOM for Enhanced Grid Stability in Renewable Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Integration of Renewable energy sources like PV in the grid is quite difficult when voltage sags and faults disrupt the grid. The Synergy in the following article is to integrate LVRT with DSTATCOM for enhanced grid stability and quality of electricity, in a synergistic way. LVRT allows PV systems to stay connected during short-term voltage downtimes and avoid disconnection, while DSTATCOM provides dynamic reactive power support to help maintain voltage and prevent power quality problems. The new system was simulated under various fault scenarios and found that it provides much better voltage stability and THD reduction by $80\%$, compared with standard LVRT or DSTATCOM systems alone. The combination of these technologies, as demonstrated by our findings, delivers higher-quality grid resilience with uninterruptible power supply. The integrated approach has proven highly relevant in new, abundantly renewable energy-intensive power grids, and provides an affordable solution to more resilient and reliable energy infrastructure.

articleTitle: An Enhancement of Power Quality in Grid-Connected Renewable Energy Systems Using Fuzzy Logic Control
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: The article represents an approach to enhance grid-connected renewable energy systems’ power quality by utilizing advanced control techniques for photovoltaic (PV) arrays and wind turbines. The maximum power point tracking method for PV arrays is neural network-based, and adaptive to changes in temperature and sunlight. This is combined with a boost converter operated through Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) and managed by a Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller to reduce oscillations and enhance response times. For wind turbines, an MPPT algorithm based on Fuzzy Logic Control (FLC) optimizes power output by adapting to wind speed changes, and a boost converter maintains voltage output for efficiency. Power synchronization from PV, wind, and thermal plants with the AC grid is achieved using a current-controlled inverter. Additionally, the unified power quality conditioner (UPQC) utilizing FLC mitigates voltage sags, swells, and harmonic distortions, improving grid stability. The performance evaluation focuses on the percentage of total harmonic distortion (THD), voltage stability, and load sensitivity, showcasing the effectiveness of these control strategies in boosting the dependability and effectiveness of renewable energy systems in conjunction with the grid, thus supporting a sustainable energy infrastructure.

articleTitle: Low Cost BCI Enabled Autonomous Wheelchair
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: The rise in spinal cord injuries (SCI) and motor neuron diseases (MND) has created an urgent need for affordable, effective assistive technologies to enhance mobility and independence for affected individuals. Traditional assistive devices are often expensive and invasive, limiting accessibility and increasing risks. This paper presents a solution: a low-cost, non-invasive Brain-Computer Interface (BCI)-enabled autonomous wheelchair system for individuals with paralysis.Using Electroencephalogram (EEG) technology, the system captures brain signals from eye blinks and facial muscle movements to navigate the wheelchair. Developed through the Incremental Prototyping Methodology, the system includes a main controller for signal acquisition and preprocessing with a Raspberry Pi 2, and a wheelchair controller that determines movement via a trained Machine Learning (ML) model. The EXG pill sensor for EEG signal acquisition enhances costeffectiveness and integration.Key innovations include low-cost BCI technology, customizable wheelchair designs, and high accuracy in interpreting EEG signals for reliable and safe movement. This approach can significantly improve the quality of life for individuals with paralysis by restoring independence and reducing reliance on caregivers.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-driven Antenna Selection Strategies for Fading MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: In this study, we investigate better performing antenna selection strategies in wireless communication systems based on machine learning algorithms. Reinforcement learning as well as neural networks among others are analysed for different metrics such a bit error rate (BER), signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and data throughput. These results show that these methods are working well against the dynamic changing of channel conditions to provide reliable and efficient. The computational complexity analysis suggests affordable overhead, allowing the feasibility of real-time implementation. Although this method can simulate the scenario in a real environment, it is not scalable due to simulation fidelity and antenna array. On the one hand, future research will refine and expand upon these ML models with real-time adaptation capabilities - On the other hand significant field trials are needed to put this work into practice for specific applications making sure that we develop robust adaptive wireless communication systems in practice.

articleTitle: Univariate Energy Consumption Forecasting in Smart Buildings using RNN & LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Forecasting energy consumption is a significant component of smart grid system stations and smart building management system. Due to significant fluctuations in the supply of power and demand, the forecast of accurate energy usage is a crucial problem for an effective energy management system. Researchers have used various methods of machine learning to address this problem. But due to the changing weather conditions and some other exogenous parameter, the results of the approaches are not good. This paper describes some existing approaches for energy forecasting with their advantages and disadvantages. The paper also proposes an appropriate type and size of dataset to be used for better forecasting of energy usage in smart buildings using two models i.e. simple recurrent neural network (RNN) and long short term memory network (LSTM) model. The findings show that LSTM performs better than RNN in terms of data with increasing trend rather than the stationary data.

articleTitle: Paper Highway Turbines Powering Traffic Management System Using IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: This study intends to develop and put into practice a unique system that uses Internet of Things technology to power a smart traffic control system by utilizing wind energy from moving cars on roads. The technology uses permanent magnet synchronous generators (PMSGs) to convert wind energy into electrical power. The wind is captured by Savonius vertical axis wind turbines (VAWTs) from any direction. Lead-acid batteries, which power LED lights and traffic control equipment including traffic signals, variable message signs, and sensors, are stored in the electrical output. Potential advantages include lower carbon emissions, increased energy resilience, and environmentally friendly transportation when wind energy is integrated into traffic control systems. IoT devices that track and optimize energy use and traffic flow are also integrated into the system. The project shows how utilizing IoT technology and renewable energy sources can create sustainable and effective urban environments, as well as how beneficial they are. But in order to overcome obstacles like erratic weather, land use, legal restrictions, and infrastructure constraints, cooperation, smart grid integration, community involvement, and policy harmonization are required. The initiative supports the expanding body of research on renewable energy sources for environmentally friendly urban planning and transportation infrastructure.

articleTitle: Amipi: Artificial Intelligence Based Interactive Humanoid Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: The main focus of this paper is to find out how the Amipi model, an Artificial Intelligence-based Interactive Humanoid Interface, can redefine human-computer interaction. By integrating advanced facial recognition, natural language processing, and gesture recognition technologies, this model offers an intuitive and immersive user experience. The system’s architecture comprises a robust Windows server for data processing and a Raspberry Pi for dynamic user interaction, ensuring real-time responsiveness. This model surpasses existing humanoid interfaces by achieving remarkable accuracy in facial recognition, natural language responsiveness, and real-time gesture interpretation. Rigorous testing has demonstrated high user satisfaction and interaction efficacy. Amipi’s potential applications span across healthcare, education, and entertainment, marking a significant advancement in intelligent interaction systems.

articleTitle: Integrated MPTA Control Framework for Hybrid Electric Vehicle Performance using Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: The world is fighting against global warming and the depletion of resources. The Adoption of hybrid technology by the automotive industry is playing an important role in making transportation sustainable, with much fewer carbon emissions. Hybrid technology will play a phenomenal role in shaping the future of transportation with ongoing research and innovation. The betterment obtained in the performance of a hybrid electric vehicle can diminish the environmental dilemmas, hence bringing about a justifiable impact and thus becoming viable for the future of transportation. The MTPA based field-oriented control should be applied for efficient operation of PMSMs as traction drives for HEVs. The proposed braking energy regenerative control strategy in the model of the hybrid electric vehicle is simulated by PSIM 2022 software. Results suggest that the proposed control strategy can aptly manage this process of braking energy regeneration leading to improved fuel efficiency and appearance. The research is conducted in a bid to demonstrate the ability of advanced control strategies towards optimization of energy management processes involved in hybrid electric vehicles; this is done for a sustainable mobility future. Finally, this paper is a positive input into the continuing development of more sustainable and efficient hybrid electric vehicles. It hence comes out as a workable solution in the transport future.

articleTitle: Harmonic Distortion Analysis of Electric Vehicle Charging Using Real-Time Data
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: The Electric Vehicle (EV) sector isundergoing rapid expansion driven by the imperative shift fromfossil fuel-dependent transportation to sustainable mobility solutions. Advanced smart charging frameworks, such as Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G), Vehicle-to-Building (V2B), and Vehicle-to-Home (V2H), are presently under development. These paradigms facilitate bidirectional energy transfer between EVs and external systems, including the electrical grid, building infrastructures, and domestic appliances. With the increasing penetration of electric vehicles, it is crucial to analyze their potential adverse influences on power quality. Therefore, the impact of electric vehicle charging on the grid must be carefully considered. This work studies the interactions of multiple electric vehicle charging through laboratory experiments. In this work, we utilized multiple electric vehicles, Electric Vehicle Chargers (EVCs), MATLAB, and Yokogawa WT1803E precision power quality analyzer to acquire real-time data. Measurements were carried out on four electric vehicles (EVs) within a local distribution grid (DG).

articleTitle: Air Purifier Automated Rover and Pollution Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Air pollution is a pressing environmental concern, particularly in densely populated urban areas, posing significant health risks to inhabitants. Traditional methods of monitoring and mitigating air pollution often fall short due to limitations in data collection, manual intervention, and outdated technologies. In response, the proposed project, Air Purifier Automated Rover and Pollution Monitoring System, presents an innovative solution by integrating robotics, Internet of Things technology, and rechargeable batteries as the primary energy source to develop an autonomous air purification and pollution monitoring system. This paper offers a comprehensive overview of the project including its objectives, methodology, hardware, software, advantages, applications, feasibility analysis etc.

articleTitle: Optimal Resource Allocation in Dynamic Fading Channels via Meta-Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: In this paper, we address the optimally dynamical resource allocation problem for fading channels utilizing meta-learning methods with an application to improve efficiency and performance in wireless communication systems. Extensive experiments are conducted and our meta-learning model has demonstrated the ability to adapt itself dynamically in various channel conditions, leading to improvement of Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR), reduction of Bit Error Rate (BER) and enhancement on throughput when compared with traditional methods. Visualizations like performance analysis comparisons, heatmaps or 3D plots are used to show how the model can be leverage as effectively manager of resources where they are and when they suit best. The performance improvements demonstrated here are statistically significant testifying for the scalability of our work. The findings of this study demonstrate the major benefits that can be achieved by meta-learning to overcome immanent issues in fast-changing wireless conditions and its potential to propel future communication technologies forward.

articleTitle: Phishing Detection Using Machine Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: In the modern world, the computer and Internet have become an entangled part of everyone’s life. The Internet is a connection of interconnected computers that can share resources, data and information all around the globe. Communication between larger distances, especially, people of different cultural background is possible with the introduction of Computer and Internet, which has helped in the economic progress of various nations. However, there are pros and cons to the Internet. While Internet is a hub of worldwide communication, one of its cons is Phishing. Phishing is an unethical and illegal activity where an attacker impersonates a real website and sends a lookalike website to people connected through Internet. Using this fake interface, private information such as Name, Address, Phone, Bank details, etc. are stolen, with the intention of stealing information for financial and other purposes. This paper presents an evaluation of varying machine learning approaches for detecting phishing.

articleTitle: Leveraging AI and ML Solutions for Secure Electric Vehicle Data Protection: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: New artificial intelligence and machine learning mechanisms have emerged recently that serve to strengthen the security systems of Electric Vehicles. Currently, they are being applied in Intrusion Detection Systems, followed by Secure Communication and Cyber-Physical System Protection. Deep learning mechanisms - particularly neural networks are primarily being used, however methods like support vector machines, decision trees, and random forests can increasingly contribute for security purposes. This review marks the important role of AI/ML in enhancing the safety of EVs, due to its capability in the most effective intrusion detection and its authentication processes as well as prevention of cyberattacks. Because these technologies can identify pattern anomalies in data sets, AI/ML can possibly detect potential security breaches beforehand. One of the most notable trends in recent developments is the integration of blockchain technology with AI/ML, which ensures advantages such as enhanced data integrity, secure communication, and improved threat detection mechanisms. As EVs become more and more connected and autonomous, the demand for advanced, proactive security measures grows exponentially. The connection of EV systems raises the risk factors by leaps and bounds, hence there is a need for AI-based security models to predict and mitigate cyber threats in real time. Future projections indicate that security paradigms will be from a reactive to proactive nature and will be driven by AI-driven models to predict cyberattacks before they occur. It would form a prime step for protection of the vehicle ecosystem, building confidence among the users, and maintaining safety and reliability for EVs. Furthermore, ongoing research and on AI/ML models can further address growing security problems as well as accommodate the speed of this technology revolution happening in the automobile industry. Adopting AI/ML and blockchain technologies can benefit protection of EVs and fortify against new rising threats.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Diagnosis Of Melanoma On Dermatoscopic Images
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Malignant melanoma is one of the common skin cancer causes for death. It occurs far less than any other skin cancer; and more likely it will be recorded and accurately diagnosed, other than any of the non-melanoma skin cancers. Melanoma is a type of skin cancer which develops as the cells responsible for producing pigment named melanocytes start to grow beyond their control. Therefore, prompt treatment along with an early diagnosis are essential. Instead, this work is focused on the multi-image technique for the diagnosis of melanoma including traditional methods based on CNN models. Overall, in this paper, three preset CNN models Resnet50 Alex Net MobileNetV2 will be combined with SVM.

articleTitle: Improving Wind Speed Forecast Accuracy with Transformer Architecture: A Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Wind energy is rapidly gaining recognition as a leading renewable energy source worldwide. Accurate forecasting of wind speed is essential for enhancing wind turbine performance, facilitating grid integration, and minimizing the uncertainties in wind energy generation. This paper presents a comparative analysis of different wind speed prediction models, specifically the Kalman Filter, Wavelet Kalman Filter, and Transformer-based models, evaluated on real-world wind speed data. To improve prediction accuracy, wavelet decomposition is used to isolate high-frequency fluctuations from the low-frequency components, creating a more refined model for wind speed forecasting. The models were trained and tested on data collected across all seasons (summer, autumn, winter, and spring) from various geographical locations, ensuring that the results are both robust and generalizable. The findings demonstrate that the proposed Transformer-based model outperforms traditional approaches such as the Kalman Filter and Wavelet Kalman Filter in both accuracy and computational efficiency. This new model achieves high prediction accuracy across all four seasons for both sites, indicating its broad applicability. The key innovation of this work lies in the development of a deep learning model based on the Transformer architecture, which effectively captures temporal dependencies and complex patterns in sequential wind data-insights that traditional models may overlook.

articleTitle: Static Modeling of MRAS for Dynamic Performance Analysis – A Simulated Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Induction machine drive is one of the decent motor drives in industrial applications. The accurate and efficient performance is a significant requirement for most of the applications. Furthermore, in close loop applications where speed control is required, hardware components increase complexity and cost, hence sensorless techniques are widely used nowadays. Model reference adaptive system (MRAS) is one of the sensorless techniques for speed estimation in which machine reference and adaptive models are used to estimate the speed. This paper elucidates the philosophy of reference frame and presents the mathematical modeling of a flux-based model reference adaptive system for indirect rotor field-oriented control (IRFOC) scheme of a three-phase induction machine (IM) drive in stationary reference frames. Analyzing the behavior of different machine states is essential for precise speed control of the machine drives particularly during transients. The novelty of this investigation is to get an in-depth knowledge of transients and performance for the improvements in MRAS based speed sensorless techniques.

articleTitle: Analysis of The Current Research Status of Reactive Power Compensation Technology for Power System Network
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: In practice, reducing reactive power to enhance system efficiency is a common objective. While this approach is generally beneficial, it can pose challenges in electrical systems that are purely resistive or capacitive. AC power systems involve the supply or consumption of two types of power: real power, which executes convenient effort, and reactive power, which provisions voltage points critical for system reliability. The management of reactive power significantly influences the security of power systems by impacting voltage stability across the network. The demand for power has surged rapidly while our generation resources remain limited. Consequently, transmission lines are becoming heavily loaded, leading to stability issues, voltage drops, and reactive power challenges. This paper explores the necessity of reactive power and various compensation techniques essential for any power system. It focuses particularly on FACTS devices like SSSC, TCR, TCSC, STATCOM, UPFC and DPFC.

articleTitle: Parkinson Prediction Using Voice Data and Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Parkinson’s disease is a prevalent neurological disorder affecting a significant portion of the global population. Early diagnosis is crucial for effective intervention and management, leading to improved patient outcomes. This study evaluates Parkinson’s disease by analyzing speech data, which typically shows distinct variations in affected individuals. Apply leverage advanced machine learning techniques and artificial intelligence to develop predictive models that can efficiently differentiate between speech data from Parkinson’s patients and healthy individuals. The model is trained on an extensive dataset of audio recordings, capturing all necessary attributes for accurate diagnosis. This work employs three machine learning algorithms K-Nearest Neighbor, Random Forest Classifier, and Decision Tree Classifier to identify the most effective model. The final approach demonstrates high efficacy in detecting Parkinson’s disease, enabling early diagnosis and personalized management strategies. This study underscores the transformative potential of machine learning and AI in Parkinson’s disease detection, presenting innovative approaches to patient care and management.

articleTitle: Facial Keypoint Detection using a Modified Convolutional Neural Network with RESNET50
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: This study introduces an attentional convolutional network for facial expression recognition, highlighting the need of facial area focus for accurate emotion detection. By using this strategy, hybrid neural networks with ResNet50 architecture show promising f advances. Visualization accentuates face traits important for detecting emotions. Using transfer learning and fine-tuning, the hybrid ResNet50 architecture collects important face features to improve emotion recognition and generalization. Although Applications such as facial recognition and emotion tracking require accurate facial keypoint detection in order to function properly. The purpose of this research is to present an improved method that makes use of a modified convolutional neural network (CNN) that is constructed on the RESNET50 architecture. Enhancing RESNET50 with particular changes allows our method to increase both the extraction of features and the localization of keypoints respectively. Typical problems that are seen in conventional CNNs are addressed by the model that has been suggested. These problems include restricted feature representation and generalization concerns. A number of exhaustive studies have demonstrated that our method delivers a greater level of accuracy and robustness in facial keypoint detection when compared to the leading methods that are currently in use. With this new development, real applications now have access to a solution that is both more effective and more scalable.

articleTitle: Optimizing Hybrid Microgrid Performance with Nonlinear Autoregressive Neural Networks in Grid-Connected and Island Mode Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Microgrids are becoming more and more significant as the electric energy industry expands into distributed power in recent years. Power quality (PQ) was quite impacted through the incorporation of renewable energy sources into the local distribution system and the nonlinear behaviour of sophisticated power electronic devices. During the micro-grid transition, the main issues are raised i.e., the supply not reached to the loads as per the demand and power quality like voltage instability, less power factor, harmonic distortions, and transients, arise. By using fuel cells, wind turbines, and photovoltaics, a single microgrid is constructed using this suggested topology’s distributed energy resources (DERs). The inverter is controlled using a nonlinear autoregressive exogenous input neural network (NARX-NN) technique to keep the power quality problems within the specified limits and to generate uninterrupted power supply in both grid connected and islanded mode operations.

articleTitle: Relay-Fuse Coordination for Enhanced Protection from Low Impedance fault in Radial Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Ensuring reliable and secure operation of power distribution networks requires effective over-current protection, which involves correct coordination between the protective devices such as fuses, circuit breaker and relays. This paper examines the coordination between relay tripping and total clearing time of fuse operation, evaluating protective devices performance as primary and backup protection mechanisms at various fault location. The simulation model is designed using PSCAD/EMTDC software, with the IEEE-13 node test feeder system serving as the basis for analysis. The study focuses on the tripping times of relays and fuses operation during low impedance shunt faults, including single-line-to-ground (LG), double-line-to-ground (LLG), and three-line-to-ground (LLLG) faults. This analysis contributes to improving the design and implementation of protection strategies in modern distribution networks.

articleTitle: Security Algorithms in Cloud Computing: Challenges and Key Discussions
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Cloud computing propose virtual, circulated, and on-demand computational services accessible worldwide. In recent years, especially following the COVID-19 pandemic, the usage of cloud computing has surged meaningfully. This technology takes facilitated remote work, enabling businesses and individuals to adopt advanced cloud-based tools to support new work environments. However, with the growing popularity of cloud computing, new challenges have emerged around data confidentiality and reliability within cloud ecosystems.
