Data is considered secure when it is classified, accessible, and intact. This paper discusses various cloud computing security algorithms and the associated challenges.

articleTitle: Impact of Integration of Renewable Energy on Protection of the Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Modern power distribution networks enhance their capacity by integrating renewable energy resources (RES). However, RES integration into traditional distribution systems poses protection challenges, such as changes in fault current and altered fault current paths. This paper investigates the impact of distributed generation (DG) on over-current protection in distribution networks. The system model has been simulated using PSCAD/EMTDC software. The IEEE-13 node test feeder system is used for performance analysis of protection system with and without photovoltaic system. The results show the impact of photovoltaic systems at different feeder locations ($25 \%, 50 \%, 75 \%$, and $100 \%$ of the length) for LG, LLG, and LLLG faults.

articleTitle: A Reliable Estimation of Solar Energy Prediction Through the use of Hybrid CNN-LSTM Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: The unpredictability of solar resources increases the difficulty of grid management as solar dispersion rates rise. Because renewable energy sources provide electricity in unpredictable and intermittent amounts, grid integration is one of the primary challenges. In order to maintain power reliability, economical delivery, and ideal entity dedication, it becomes essential to anticipate solar electricity. Every year, new methods and strategies are developed worldwide to improve forecast accuracy and minimize uncertainty in models. To address this, a unique hybrid deep learning technique based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and long short-term memory (LSTM) is suggested. Solar energy generation predictive performance is determined by use of statistical measurements, including root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), normalized RMSE, relative RMSE, and coefficient of determination ($R^{2}$). When comparing the proposed model with current models, the model’s higher prediction accuracy is evident from lower statistical metrics. These indicators demonstrate the model’s increased capacity for precise prediction-making and serve as trustworthy gauges of its effectiveness. The continually lower results for each evaluation criterion suggest that forecasting accuracy and reliability, which are essential in many different applications and industries, may be improved.

articleTitle: Patient Data Management Using Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: In this paper, a healthcare data management system based on blockchain is introduced, aiming to improve patient-centered care and streamline the handling of healthcare data. The system makes use of smart contracts deployed on a blockchain network to securely store and oversee patient information, such as visit details, test results, and other health-related data. When a patient visits the hospital, a new smart contract is generated if one is not already in place, ensuring that each patient has a dedicated and unchangeable record of their medical history. The system’s capability to prevent unauthorized alterations to patient data by medical professionals is one of its main benefits. Staff at the hospital is given permission to use the system, enabling them to input new health information into a patient’s smart contract. Furthermore, patients can access a duplicate of their data, which encourages transparency and empowers them to actively engage in their healthcare journey. The system is equipped with a user-friendly interface that includes features like the ability to see all patients in the hospital and search for specific patients using a search bar, streamlining the management and retrieval of data. The purpose of implementing this system based on blockchain is to tackle issues concerning data security, accessibility, and interoperability within healthcare environments. Through the use of blockchain technology, the system guarantees the integrity, privacy, and protection against unauthorized changes of data, thereby promoting trust among involved parties and leading to enhanced healthcare results.

articleTitle: Design of particle swarm optimization for the measurement of Contact resistance and cut-off frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: OTFTs, or organic thin-film transistors, are very flexible, low-cost semiconductors used in printing, detecting, and displaying application. OTFTs have certain disadvantages despite these advantages, including low cutoff frequency or velocity, high contact resistance, An objective function trained by particle swarm optimization (PSO) has been developed to tackle these problems. The overall performance will be assessed at various channel lengths (length of source and drain electrode) by increasing the contact length. Moreover, scaling the contact length shows that PSO provided the highest cut-off frequency and lowest contact resistance value compared toother methods. Moreover, a drop in contact resistance and an increase in cut-off frequency persist for longer contact length scaling in the about 80 nm range.

articleTitle: Advanced Resource Management in Fog Computing Vehicular Networks using Hybrid PSO and Min-Max Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: The integration of IoV and FC abates congestion on roads, increased transport effectiveness, and privacy in vehicular networks. NOMA technology enhances the spectral efficiency and access capacity of network: However, the existing IoV infrastructure is failing to cop up with the modern need for intelligent transportation due to its low scalability and high data burden. An Allocation Framework for Hybrid Resources in NOMA-based Fog Computing Vehicular Networks (FCVR) Employing Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Min-Max Techniques. This involves simulations of NOMA-based Fog Computing Vehicular Network and resource allocation through Min-Max and PSO techniques. The approach to be taken will be to evaluate ergodic capacities. This invention provides a robust solution, thus, can be customized in a dynamical vehicular environment and lays down the future groundwork for research on how to enhance fog computing applications over VANETs.

articleTitle: Early Diabetes Prediction Using CNN-LSTM and CNN-Bi-LSTM Models Optimized with Adam on the PIMA Indian Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Early detection of the condition is critical to proper diabetes management and reducing risk for complications. A new concept for early prediction of diabetes is proposed in this study where the LSTM and CNN models are combined with Bi-LSTM. The target is to use the Adam optimizer for these models on top of improving this model, and testing it onto the PIMA Indian Diabetes Dataset. The CNNLSTM model is particularly well-suited for time dependent data as it has been designed to extract the spatial patterns from an input and in turn record memory of a problem across time steps. Meanwhile, with the data from both past and future, the CNN-Bi-LSTM model is capable of better prediction. From our experimental results, we can see that these hybrid models achieve superior performance over traditional machine learning algorithms and hence could serve as a powerful resource for predicting diabetes at an early stage. Thus the application of this approach is a new challenge and seems to have potential for improving early diagnosis in order to implement timely interventions in diabetes care.

articleTitle: Advanced Malware Classification Using Convolutional Neural Networks and Image Transformation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Malware seriously compromises cybersecurity and calls for sophisticated and effective categorization methods to find and lessen its effects. This research article offers a complete method based on image processing and deep learning to classify malware. ResNet18, VGG16, VGG19, AlexNet, and our custom-designed MalwareNet are among the several deep learning models we use to categorize malware photos from the nine different classes in the Big 2015 dataset-which shows a clear class imbalance. Using hyperband and bayesian optimization approaches, our strategy maximizes hyperparameters to provide the greatest performance. The hyperparameters for ResNet18, VGG16, VGG19, and AlexNet models comprise learning rate, kernel size, number of epochs, dropout rate, and dense layer size as well as particular parameters for MalwareNet including the number of neurons in each layer and the fully connected layer size. With MalwareNet obtaining especially remarkable results, the examination of our models shows great accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 scores. We examine the training accuracy, F1 score, and log loss measures in great detail; we then show the classification performance over all classes using confusion matrices. With notable increases in malware detection and categorization, the suggested model offers a strong and practical answer for uses in cybersecurity. Supported by diligent hyperparameter adjustment and performance evaluation, this work expands the field by providing a comprehensive comparison of many deep learning architectures and how effectively they classify malware. The results show how well deep learning models might improve malware detection systems and protect digital environments against hostile attacks.

articleTitle: An Improved Method to Find Location and Sizing of DG In IEEE-69 Bus Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Getting more power is seen as one of the fastest effective means for nations to develop and one of the greatest challenges in the world at present. Countries have changed their strategies for utilizing renewable energies rather than nonrenewable sources of energy since there aren’t many of them and utilizing them is terrible for the environment. Renewable energies are easy to get, never lose worth over time, and don’t depend on fluctuations in price. This means they can be used more in energy systems today. The electrical grid will have to change because of the most suitable location to position these resources and the best way to utilizethem. There is an approach to sort through which and how large to put DG (distributed generation) in energy distribution networks so that there is as little energy reduction, voltage-age constraints, distributed generation loading constraints, current limits, and distributed generation in filtration constraints as possible. In the first step, you need to find the distributed generation feature that helps each bus the most. After that, pick the best spot for the distributed generation to ensure it helps every bus most effectively. This method is able to be used to figure out the number and location of both single and multiple DG. For determining the most suitable area for, size and power factor of distributed generation in the distributional structure, the Coot Bird Optimization Technique (CBOM) is proposed. The suggested method has been tested on Distributed Networking and IEEE 69-bus. The CBOM method that was mentioned is a good way to determine the best place, terms of sizes and power factors for distributed creation. It could also be used for other kinds of distribution structures.

articleTitle: “Liver Disease Risk Prediction Using Regularized Deep Learning: A Novel Approach”
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Liver diseases are common, thereby posing a significant quality-of-life impairment. They have required accurate and prompt assessments to be managed. Typically, conventional methods of evaluation often include subjectivity and laborious amounts of work. It introduces a DNN-based model with L2 regularization to predict risk categorization of liver diseases based on five categories of categorizations: Healthy_Liver, Low_Risk, Moderate_Risk, High_Risk, and Severe_Liver_Disease. The model includes the hidden layers with rectified linear unit (ReLU) activation functions, batch normalization, and dropout for regularizing to achieve robust learning. The DNN was trained in a very comprehensive Kaggle dataset with many physiological and biochemical features and has achieved an impressive 94.07% classification accuracy. Healthcare professionals will be equipped with a significant resource to develop personalized treatment strategies facilitated by this investigation, which highlights the capabilities of deep learning methodologies in the automation of liver disease assessment. Subsequent research will focus on integrating additional data sources to improve the model’s scalability and predictive precision, thus promoting the advancement of automated liver disease evaluation in clinical settings.

articleTitle: Overcoming Barriers: Understanding and Addressing Impediments to Electric Vehicle Adoption in India
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: The transition to electric vehicles (EVs) in India is essential for addressing environmental concerns and reducing dependence on fossil fuels. However, numerous barriers impede the widespread adoption of EVs in the country. The paper aims to highlight factors that influence electric vehicle adoption, including lack of charging infrastructure, consumer anxieties, and OEM related constraints. Through a comprehensive examination of these impediments, the paper proposes strategies to overcome them and accelerate EV adoption. These strategies encompass policy interventions, infrastructure development, and awareness campaigns. By understanding and addressing these challenges, India can pave the way for a more sustainable and eco-friendly transportation ecosystem, thereby contributing to the global efforts to combat climate change and promote clean energy adoption.

articleTitle: Cardiovascular Disease Analysis and Diagnosis Using Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Coronary disease, a predominant factor contributing to illness and death on a global scale, often exhibits diverse symptoms. For the timely intervention and enhanced patient results, early and precise prediction of coronary disease based on symptoms is crucial. New ways of predicting coronary disease have been enabled through developments in Machine learning (ML) with respect to symptom data. This research explores the use of machine learning approaches over a UCI dataset to predict the likelihood of having coronary disease. The dataset comes from UCI ML Repository with diverse patient health, lifestyle and medical history features. Methods include dataset analysis inclusive of data exploration, preprocessing, and feature engineering. Filling in missing values, encoding categorical variables, and normalizing numerical attributes are some of the ways that prepare the dataset for modeling purposes. Further, splitting the data into training and testing sets before using some ML algorithms to generate predictive models. These models are then evaluated using normal classification metrics like precision, accuracy, F score and recall. For every model hyper-parameter tuning is applied after which feature importance is investigated to pinpoint key elements concerning prediction of cases having coronary diseases respectively. The study contributes to the data-driven approaches for cardiovascular health and underscores the potential of machine learning in augmenting traditional diagnostic methods.

articleTitle: Cell Temperature Estimation In Lithium Ion Cell for Electric Two-Wheeler Application In Indian Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Green mobility is the thrust around the world to make transportation environmentally sustainable. Electric vehicles (EVs) are emerging as the front-runner in green technology-based transportation systems. Lithium-based battery technologies are backing the emergence of electric vehicles. High energy density and longer cycle life are the prominent characteristics of Li-ion cells, making them wellsuited for EV applications. However, the optimum performance of the battery pack is highly subjected to the operating temperature. India is emerging as a hub of electric vehicles, especially for electric two-wheelers and e-rickshaws. The temperature in the summer of India reaches up to $50{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ or even more in some cases, which is beyond the optimum operating range of Li-ion cells. It becomes necessary to estimate the cell temperature so that safe operation can be ensured. This paper aims to assess the temperature rise of the 18650 Li -ion cell under the real-world drive cycle specifically developed for electric scooter applications for the city of Lucknow, India. The thermal model based on Joule’s heating is simulated using Matlab Simulink. A comparison of simulated cell temperature rise is done for real-world drive cycle and standard drive cycles such as the IDC and WLTC. The comparison of results indicates the need to incorporate the real driving behavior during the thermal modeling of the cell as the standard drive cycles underestimate the temperature rise by many folds.

articleTitle: Disparity-constrained Knowledge Distillation for Cyber-Physical Systems and Edge Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Miniscule wearable devices with vast data from Cyber-Physical Systems and Internet of Things face challenges in storage, power, and compute due to limited resources. To adapt the state-of-the-art pre-trained models, models and data need to be processed using compression techniques like Knowledge Distillation for its application on edge devices. Knowledge Distillation is limited by student-teacher learning capabilities and several limitations highlighted in introduction. This paper introduces a novel experimental investigation on the impact of size and structural disparity on the performance of knowledge distillation in wearable devices which are otherwise deprived form using these for the given constraints. It uses 12 models of different sizes and architectures as student and teacher networks to distil knowledge from scratch utilizing image augmentation, random subsampling, and checkpoint restoration of student models while training from differently-abled teacher networks to quantify the best accuracy of distilled models at varying size and structural-disparities. The study shows that selecting models with smaller size and structural disparity can significantly enhance the accuracy of knowledge distilled models. The authors suggest further research to develop a new metric for these disparities, which can help identify potential teachers for students constrained by storage and compute limits. We achieved some significant results on standard benchmark datasets like CIFAR10, FMNIST and MNIST that demonstrate that knowledge-distilled models’ accuracy can be improved by selecting student-teacher models with smaller size and structural disparity and suggests further research to develop a new metric.)

articleTitle: Machine Learning Enabled FBG Optical Sensor Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: This review paper develops the current understanding of machine learning applications in the Structural health monitoring industry using Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) sensors. We describe how this synergy transforms strain measuring, temperature sensing, and structural health monitoring based on analysis of papers and case studies. In addition to aspects involving these sensors, the discussion of how integration can achieve accuracy, real-time capabilities, and predictive analytics also raises issues with data management complexity, the efficiency of the algorithms to be used, and the efficiency of integrating this into current systems. This research paper also presents a comprehensive investigation into using FBG optical sensor technology and machine learning models for the early detection and management of diabetes mellitus. Thus, as we suggest possible solutions and directions of further research in the form of conclusions, it seems to us that a growing trend will make in aviation operations safer than ever and more efficient.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Driven Load Balancing in Software Defined Networks: Recent Progress and Emerging Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Load balancing has arisen as an important challenge in case of Software Defined Network because of the dynamic patterns in the traffic and expanding demands of network. The centralized framework of SDN delivers unique opportunity. It enhances the performance of network and usage of resources by distributing the load of network dynamically across multiple devices and paths. This paper provides a concise overview of SDN and examines the influence of load balancing within this context. It includes a comprehensive study to analyse the algorithms of load balancing used by researchers for different scenarios and to identify the persistent challenges. Furthermore, a methodology has been proposed to highlight the impact of machine learning techniques to amplify the load balancing decision which can be useful to develop more intelligent and adaptive architectures of SDN. For future research, the study aims to deploy scalable and robust SDN solutions in next-generation network infrastructures.

articleTitle: Sustainable Energy and IoT Based Highway Lighting Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: This paper proposes a smart highway lighting system powered by sustainable and energy storage devices. The system uses microcontroller-based master-slave node combination mechanism for energy harvesting. As an added advantage, the Air Quality Index (AQI) in real time is monitored using an additional node MCU. The roadway lights are powered by batteries that are charged during the day by the solar or wind energy system. The microcontroller maximizes energy consumption and monitor’s system performance. Using a sensor, the extra node MCU continually checks the air quality and provides real-time data to provide a safe environment for walkers and automobiles. The system’s adaptive lighting function further optimizes energy economy by adjusting brightness and lighting schedules based on traffic volume, weather, and availability of natural light using a variety of IR and LDR sensors. The presented system is verified in simulation platform and at the same time a prototype model of the presented system is also implemented.

articleTitle: Modern Agriculture: A Review of Emerging Crop Yield Prediction Models Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Accurately predicting crop yields is a very critical component of global food safety and agricultural efficiency. Such is a multifaceted approach toward crop yield prediction explored in the present study. Anchoring on the Green Revolution and subsequent impact on crop diversity and resilience, it reviews how far a wide range of yield prediction models has evolved in terms of effectiveness, including regression models, machine learning, and hybrid models. Such methods would require advanced machine learning techniques, statistical methods, and integration of data sources like satellite imagery and meteorological data to assure the accuracy of yield predictions. This study analyzes strengths and limitations of the models in order to provide a fuller understanding of the current situation and identify opportunities for technological advances and improved implementation strategies in crop yield forecasting.

articleTitle: Emerging Security Challenges in Advanced Cloud Computing Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Cloud computing is a archetype that permits users to access a shared pool of computing resources on an on-demand or pay-per-use basis. It offers numerous benefits to individuals and organizations, including significant cost savings in both capital and operational expenditures. However, there are several obstacles that prevent widespread adoption of cloud computing, with security being a major concern. Insufficient security measures can have negative consequences for this computing model, consequential in individual, ethical, and economic harm. The security issues that various cloud entities—such as cloud facility providers, data holders, and cloud users—face will be covered in this paper. It will specifically focus on the crypto-cloud, which encompasses various aspects of announcement, multiplication, and service level agreements (SLAs). By examining the causes and effects of different cyber-attacks, the paper aims to propose necessary security enhancements.

articleTitle: Heart Condition Monitoring Using Phonocardiogram and Murmurs Analysis by CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Heart failure is the leading cause of mortality worldwide. Cardiac auscultation is one of the oldest diagnostic methods to explore the condition of the heart. Mechanical activities of heart initiated by biopotentials generated by the Sino-Atrium (SA) node of the heart causes non-stationery and non-deterministic signals commonly known as Heart Sound Signal (HSS) and the graphical representation of HSS is termed as Phonocardiogram (PCG) while recorded by an electronic stethoscope. When assessing a variety of cardiac anomalies, like valvular heart disease, irregular heartbeat, cardiac decompensation, and anatomical flaws in heart, PCG can offer extremely useful diagnostic data. The first and second (S1, S2) heart sounds, which are often the two loudest heart sounds, make up PCG. The PCG signal can contain murmurs, the third and fourth cardiac sounds (S3), and other unusual noises including clicks, snaps, and rubs in both pathological and non-pathological circumstances. Analysis of PCG thus becomes very effective in diagnosing the cardiovascular disorder, if any, in a non-invasive manner. The basic aim of the thesis is to develop an Automatic Computerized Auscultation (ACA) for effective and efficient status monitoring of the condition of the heart. ACA is a non-invasive, cost effective, fast and accurate method that may assist the physicians in early detection of cardiac illness truncating the death rate due to cardio vascular diseases by providing diagnostic and prognostic information. The proposed CNN method deals with classification of heart murmurs as innocent (normal) and pathological (abnormal) following the same stages of classification of heart sound. The best combination for murmur classification provided a classification AUC of 9345551.

articleTitle: Recent Developments in Botnet Detection Tools and Techniques for IoT Security: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) embodies a paradigm shift in technology, connecting a diverse array of devices to enhance operational efficiency and user convenience across industries, educational settings, and urban infrastructures. This paper provides an in-depth examination of IoT’s evolution, showcasing its profound impact on transforming traditional practices through interconnected smart systems. Despite its numerous advantages, the widespread adoption of IoT introduces significant challenges in cyber security and privacy. Recent high-profile cyber-attacks have underscored vulnerabilities inherent in IoT networks. This study delves into the growing threat of IoT botnets, sophisticated networks of compromised devices exploited by malicious actors for largescale attacks. It explores cutting-edge detection methodologies, including advanced deep learning models and architectural frameworks such as IoT-BDA, designed to proactively identify and mitigate these emerging threats. By critically analyzing current methodologies and technological innovations, this research aims to bolster awareness and develop robust strategies to safeguard IoT ecosystems. Ultimately, these efforts seek to establish a secure foundation that fosters continuous innovation and sustainable development within the IoT landscape.

articleTitle: Securing The Internet of Vehicles (IoVs): Review of Machine Learning Techniques for Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Interconnectivity in the Internet of Vehicles (IoVs), enabled by its development and implementation in real-world, facilitates seamless communication between vehicles, infrastructure, and backend systems but also introduces important cybersecurity risks, with malware posing a dangerous threat. Conventional security solutions that rely on signature-based detection, fail against new variants. This current study explores Machine Learning (ML) as a proactive solution for enhancing detection in IoVs systems. Through investigation of new studies, the current study, aims to explore various ML approaches for IoVs malware uncovering, including supervised, unsupervised, and deep learning techniques. It evaluates their effectiveness, strengths, and limitations in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and flexibility. These novel techniques analyze specific features, ensuring accurate detection of malware during the analysis process. The study meticulously divides both traditional-based approaches and ML methodologies, considering findings from previous and recent research papers. Research conclusions derived from rigorous experiments are evaluated, and algorithm performances are systematically compared based on accuracy detection. As the massive implementation of IoVs depends on the ability to establish trust and confidence against evolving cyber threats, it becomes imperative, making the integration of advanced security measures, particularly those rooted in ML to enhance security against malware threats in IoVs network.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Optimization Of EV Charging Station Converters: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: This study takes up the potential of artificial intelligence in enhancing the power conversion at electric vehicle charging stations. With the increasing trend of efficient usage of electric and hybrid electric vehicles, smart and efficient charging solutions for these vehicles are gaining wide acceptance. In this context, a few AI techniques, such as machine learning and neural networks, shall be applied to optimize the performance of converters used at the charging stations. Strategies provided include AI-driven adaptable strategies to varying energy demands and an integrated capacity in the power grid, both to minimize energy losses. The focus is on increasing energy transfer efficiency, reducing electricity waste, and lowering costs for operators and users, rather than solely accelerating charging speeds. The integration of AI in EV charging technology is the route toward making charging systems smart and efficient, as the charge from the technology meets the demands of the futuristic vehicle users and the energy sector in general.

articleTitle: Serverless Cloud Computing: Navigating Challenges and Exploring Future Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Serverless cloud computing stands out for its remarkable benefits, including cost reduction, scalability enhancement, and increased efficiency. This paper provides an in-depth analysis of significant shortcomings in serverless cloud computing, such as cold start latency, vendor lock-in, and the general lack of control over the cloud environment. This research introduces innovative approaches to address the major pitfalls of serverless cloud computing. Advanced machine learning-based optimization algorithms are proposed to predict and pre-warm functions, by significantly reducing latency. Additionally, a comprehensive AI-driven security framework is developed that continuously monitors for anomalies, providing robust protection and ensuring data integrity. This approach ensures low-latency processing and improved real-time performance by combining serverless architecture with edge computing. Overall, it serves as a roadmap for the future of serverless cloud computing, highlighting the pivotal role in shaping the technological landscape and setting new standards for the industry.

articleTitle: Key Safety Design Overview in AI-driven Autonomous and Battery-electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: With the increasing presence of autonomous SAE level 3 and level 4, which incorporate artificial intelligence software, along with the complex technical challenges they present, it is critical to maintain a strong focus on functional safety and robust software design. This paper explores the necessary safety architecture and systematic approach for automotive software and hardware, including fail-soft handling of automotive safety integrity level (ASIL) D (highest level of safety integrity), adoption of machine learning (ML), and artificial intelligence (AI) in automotive safety architecture. By addressing the unique challenges presented by increasing AI-based automotive software, we proposed various techniques, such as mitigation strategies and safety failure analysis, to enforce safety compliance and reliability of automotive software, as well as the role of AI in software reliability throughout the data lifecycle.

articleTitle: Exploring the Cloud and Fog: Addressing Security Risks in AI Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: There are various security risks with cloud- or fog-based machine learning services. Because machine learning applications rely on these services, it is imperative to secure the underlying cloud or fog services to prevent serious disruptions to the applications. We distinguish based on whether Artificial Intelligence applications are employed in a fog computing network or the cloud because the needs for these applications can also vary. This consequently gives rise to various threats or avenues for attack. Security responsibilities for cloud platforms can be split up amongst several parties. Even though fog computing networks have fewer responsibilities, we still need to safeguard services from physical access to the devices at the network’s edge because they have been moved there. Lastly, we go into specific information security requirements for AI-related applications.

articleTitle: Object Detection: A comprehensive study of famous Deep Learning approaches with case study of Helmet Detection dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: An important challenge of computer vision, object detection is critical to numerous uses, such as augmented reality, autonomous driving, and monitoring. To provide a concise example on helmet detection, this paper discusses the latest deep learning architectures for the object detection task. Thus, using a number of data sets the performance of such models as YOLO, SSD, R-CNN is estimated as thoroughly as possible. Our work provides both the strengths and weakness of each technique for object detection in different contexts and scales based on comprehensive investigations and comparisons. This study further enriches the existing knowledge base and possibilities for the field of not only object detection but also demonstrates potential implications of the methodology within the real-world scenarios. We emphasize the importance of accurate object detection and also present useful information for other authors who focuses on creating better models. The last case of applying object detection is helmet detection, where object detection can be used to enforce compliance with safety rules at construction sites or in traffic monitoring. In the real-time detection, we discovered that YOLO offered higher accuracy because of its speed, making it better than the other models, whereas, SSD served as a better compromise between accuracy and speed as opposed to other models. R-CNN was faster but less accurate, while the much more accurate F-FR-CNN was slower and more computationally expensive. Our results indicate that it is highly dependent on the intended application, whether in need of real-time evaluation or accuracy. For future work it is recommended to further adapt these models to run on edge-devices and afforded to provide insights for enhancing their resilience under varying environmental conditions so as to support their practical uses in real-world applications.

articleTitle: A Secure Cryptosystem for Secure Data Transmission in IoT-based UAV Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a transformative technology that connects devices and objects embedded with sensors through the Internet. IoT-based UAV networks prove their better utilization in military operations, agriculture, smart cities, etc. Besides providing better coverage, the UAVs carry sensitive data in the resource-constrained environment during communication with the user entity, which makes them vulnerable to logical and physical attacks. Considering the challenges, we propose a secure cryptosystem for secure data transmission in IoT-based UAV Networks, which employs the hyperelliptic curve of genus greater than one, providing better performance in terms of computation, communication, and storage costs. The cryptosystem secures the user’s private key while transmitting sensitive information using a hyperelliptic curve discrete logarithmic problem (HCDLP). It achieves security features such as anonymity, untraceability, forward secrecy and others using a secure hash function, random number and separate timestamps to prevent physical and logical attacks, which are analysed using formal verification Scyther tool and informal method. The proposed cryptosystem performance is compared with benchmark schemes, and the result shows lower computation, communication and storage costs as $10.33 \mathrm{~ms}, 1456$ bits and 1280 bits, respectively, with no trade-off between security and performance.

articleTitle: Supervised Machine Learning Techniques in the Improvement of Performance of Solar PV Systems due to Partial Shading
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: This paper aims to propose a method for using artificial neural networks to enhance the efficiency of solar PV systems under partially shaded conditions. It examines three system sizes ($4 \times 4,5 \times 5$, and $6 \times 4$) allows for flexibility in design, catering to varying energy needs and space constraints and various connection methods: These include Series-parallel (SP), Total-cross-tied (TCT), Bridge-link (BL), Honeycomb (HC), and SP-TCT, BL-TCT or HC-TCT by using MATLAB/SIMULINK. Analyze training state plots, performance plots, error histograms, and regression plots to assess these configurations. The findings revealed that integrating neural networks improves the performance of solar PV systems in shaded conditions, mainly through improved decision-making about how to complement energy derived from panels. Combinations with TCT and other traditional techniques yielded the highest results among all company sizes. From the training state plot, it is evident that the neural network model is stable, and converging very well from the performance plot showing good prediction. Working with the error histogram and observing only minor deviations in the predicted output; the regression plot shows a strong, positive correlation between the predicted and the actual values.

articleTitle: Cybersecurity strategies for protecting smart grid in Residential building complex from attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: The addition of digital technology to energy systems, smart grids have been created, which make power delivery more reliable, efficient, and long-lasting. But this progress comes with big security risks, especially in apartment buildings with lots of smart devices and monitors that are all connected to each other. This paper looks at important cybersecurity methods that can be used to protect smart grid infrastructure in residential settings from cyberattacks. Some of the main goals are to protect important assets, keep data private and secure, make sure communication networks are safe, and make sure systems can handle attacks. Strong access controls, ongoing monitoring, and effective incident response methods are all part of the suggested procedures that put a high focus on lowering risks and keeping the smart grid running. The study also stresses how important it is to follow rules, teach users, and encourage smart grid components to work together. By following these thorough cybersecurity steps, smart grid security and dependability in homes may be kept, which will eventually lead to a safer and more resilient energy environment.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Bagging Classifiers Between Multi-Core And Single-Core Processors Using Python Multiprocessing
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: In recent years, the demand for efficient and scalable machine learning algorithms has surged. Bagging (Bootstrap Aggregating) stands out as a widely used ensemble technique that combines multiple base classifiers to enhance predictive accuracy and mitigate over fitting. However, when implementing bagging classifiers in Python, a crucial consideration lies in their effective utilization of multi-core processors. Python, as a language, faces parallelism limitations due to the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) present in its C implementation (cPython). The GIL restricts Python threads from fully exploiting multiple CPU cores, thereby limiting their concurrency. Consequently, relying solely on regular threads for concurrency would not fully harness the potential of multi-core processors. Python, as a language, faces parallelism limitations due to the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) present in its C implementation (cPython). The GIL restricts Python threads from fully exploiting multiple CPU cores, thereby limiting their concurrency. Consequently, relying solely on regular threads for concurrency would not fully harness the potential of multi-core processors. To overcome this limitation, we recommend leveraging Python’s multiprocessing module. Unlike threads, which share the same memory space and are subject to the GIL, multiprocessing creates separate processes, each with its own Python interpreter instance. As a result, these processes can run in parallel, effectively utilizing multiple CPU cores. Our study delves into the performance comparison of bagging classifiers on multi-core processors versus single-core using Python multiprocessing. Our experiments reveal that multiprocessing significantly improves execution time, particularly for CPU-bound tasks. By leveraging multiple cores, bagging classifiers can better generalize to unseen data and achieve enhanced predictive accuracy.

articleTitle: Exploring Multidisciplinary Data Visualization and Data Analysis with R
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: R is a proprietary programming language that has a large ecosystem of packages for data exploration and visualization, as well as strong community support. This article investigates a wide range of topics, including trend visualizations using the R programming language, sentiment analysis on Twitter, and basic voltage detection and frequency anomalies. It talks about the impact of sentiment analysis on various sensors and presents the PeakValley algorithm for real-time grid event analysis. In order to visualize load profiles and find trends in consumption, Ris employed multiple linear regression.The cgmquantify package for glucose data in Python and R is evaluated, as is the integration of the FacebookAPI with R for social network analysis.The paper also discusses big data categorization in medicine, R’s interface with Hadoop for digital libraries, and Weka, RapidMiner, and R for time series analysis in structural health monitoring. It highlights R’s adaptability and recommends that future studies concentrate on improving realtime processing, integrating machine learning, and visualizing techniques.

articleTitle: A Review of Traffic Management: Real-Time Monitoring and Dynamic Control
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: India, at present the largest democracy in the world, has the second largest network of roads globally, but it is failing miserably to contain traffic in its rapidly growing cities. The traditional thinking in traffic control fails to provide solutions for the burgeoning car ownership, the expanding scope of urban streets, and the peculiarities of the environment. This paper looks at the current traffic management technologies which include RFID, VANETs, energy harvesting, and adaptive traffic control systems and their advantages and disadvantages. To overcome these drawbacks, we propose a traffic management system that consists of sound and vibration sensors, piezoelectric energy harvesting, edge computing, and the EDF algorithm for dynamic signal control. The use of Augmented Reality (AR) displays will enable drivers to receive real-time traffic information and so enrich their driving experience. This system aims at providing effective traffic flow, reduction of traffic jams, increased sustainability through low reliance on external power and real time conditions. The potential future work should be aimed at enhancing the algorithms of machine learning, increasing energy effectiveness and achieving better security and system scalability. Hence, to guarantee long-term sustainability of smart traffic management systems in dynamic context of urban scenario

articleTitle: The Impact of AI on the Widespread Use of EV’s: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Energy production on a worldwide scale is now dependent on nonrenewable fossil fuels such as coal, oil, and gas. These fuels are known to contribute to climate change, escalate geopolitical conflicts, deplete already scarce resources, and have negative impacts on human health. So, the Paris Agreement is only one example of how major international environmental organizations and nations have responded to the threat of climate change by establishing programs and policies to curb emissions of carbon. In the last ten years, there have been tremendous advancements in both academic study and commercialization related to renewable power production and vehicle electrification. Electric cars currently only account for a fraction of the market, even though they provide several benefits to the environment and drivers’ performance compared to conventional vehicles. The increased initial investment, shorter range, and absence of supporting infrastructure are the key reasons why electric cars (EVs) do not attract the same level of customer interest as traditional internal combustion vehicles. In order to address the significant initial investment, it is crucial to reduce the cost of the electric vehicle’s battery pack. To improve battery production efficiency and find inexpensive, high-performing battery materials, machine learning offers a time- and moneysaving solution. With the help of AI algorithms and controls, we can maximize energy saving, get a more accurate estimate of the vehicle’s driving range, and alleviate “range anxiety” among consumers. Electric cars might be more appealing to consumers if charging stations are conveniently located and the smart grid is in place. Smart grid technology known as vehicle-to-grid (V2G) allows electric vehicle owners to generate income by supplying electricity to the grid. Recent developments in electric vehicles (EVs) and associated infrastructure, driven largely by advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), have increased the allure of EVs to consumers. Using AI to enhance electric vehicles, make smart grid integration easier, and improve electric vehicle charging stations is examined and evaluated critically. We conclude by looking forward to potential trends and developments in the field.

articleTitle: New Era of IoT with Cloud Computing: A review of Technology, Issues and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: The convergence of Internet of Things (IoT) and cloud computing has unleashed unprecedented opportunities across various domains, revolutionizing industries, and redefining the way we interact with technology. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the symbiotic relationship between IoT and cloud computing, exploring the technological advancements, key issues, and challenges in this transformative landscape. The review begins by elucidating the foundational concepts of IoT and cloud computing, highlighting their synergistic potential. Subsequently, it examines the integration of IoT devices with cloud infrastructure. Furthermore, the paper delves into the technological enablers such as edge computing, fog computing, and serverless architectures that augment the capabilities of IoT-cloud ecosystems. However, alongside these advancements, critical issues and challenges emerge, encompassing security and privacy concerns, interoperability issues, data management complexities, and regulatory compliance. The review elucidates these challenges in detail, offering insights into potential mitigation strategies and future research directions. In addition, the paper discusses emerging trends such as AI-driven IoT applications.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approaches to Securing IoT Networks: A Comprehensive Review of Recent Advances
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: The IoT is a network of physical objects embedded with sensors and software, connecting and exchanging data over the internet. With over 7 billion connected devices, experts predict growth to 10 billion by 2020 and 22 billion by 2025. Machine learning ML technologies are advancing quickly, with new algorithms and approaches emerging regularly. In this paper, a review is carried out that helps provide insights into their effectiveness in the current landscape. Different ML techniques are categorized and evaluated based on how they address diverse challenges. Reviewing current ML techniques helps in understanding their strengths and limitations in combating novel attack vectors. Later on, a comparative analysis of these techniques is conducted based on performance metrics. A comprehensive review identifies gaps in current research and practice, highlighting areas where ML techniques might need further development or improvement.

articleTitle: Review on Equivalent Circuit and Data driven approaches for Electric Vehicle Battery Models
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Batteries play a crucial role in electric vehicle development (EV).In EV batteries real-time state estimation is challenging and hence is approximated indirectly. In this paper, a comparative review of state estimation techniques and battery models is conducted. The Equivalent Circuit Model (ECM) is found more appropriate since it achieves a balance between computing efficiency and accuracy. While chemistry-based models are more accurate than ECMs, however, for practical uses a trade-off is essential. In this paper the data-driven state estimation approaches are also reviewed. In depth analysis of dynamical equations are not required in data driven models, but are better at capturing non-linearities, are adaptable, and can be generalized to different case scenarios. Data-driven techniques are also less sensitive to parameter uncertainty and are capable of learning from data. This paper concludes by emphasizing the need for trade-off between real-time applicability and accuracy by focusing on the ECMs and data driven models.

Author Keywords: state estimation and State of Charge

articleTitle: Reliability and Cost Consideration in the Design of the Electric Vehicle Charging Station's Intermediately Facilitated Ports
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Manufacturing companies are prioritizing customer charging infrastructure as Electric Vehicles (EVs) attain a higher level of popularity. In small EV charging situations, charging port reliability is difficult to ensure, even while charging station companies follow distribution system standards. In order to enhance the reliability of the charging station for the distribution system, the implementation of 24-ported configurations has been suggested, and systems have been developed with the individual batch structure. The reliability of the suggested identical and non-identical port designs has been evaluated by analyzing the failure rate of each individual port in a batch. The failure rate of the proposed configuration with 24 ports has been assessed according to the MILHBK-217F book requirements. The evaluation process has been implemented to determine the success rate of the charging station based on the failure rate of the port. The maintenance cost has been calculated using the failure and success rate of the proposed 24-port system. Ultimately, the evaluation of the suggested 24-port setups has been conducted to determine their failure rate, success rate, and maintenance cost. This study utilizes the binomial distribution probability technique to accurately estimate the failure rate of the charging station. The proposed 24-port layouts, whether identical or non-identical, are capable of ensuring reliable operation and may be implemented in the limited space available for the installation of EV charging stations.

Author Keywords: Voltage stability of the charging station

articleTitle: AAWAS: An Application and Workload-Aware Scheduling Technique for Efficient Task Allocation in Cloud Computing Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: One interesting aspect of distributed systems is cloud computing. It offers its services on an as-needed, pay-per-use basis. Research challenges in cloud computing include the scheduling and balance of tasks. Scheduling tasks entails assigning them to available resources (Virtual Machines), whereas load balancing is spreading out the work over multiple available resources. We offer a job scheduling technique that takes into account anticipated demands on compute nodes. We begin by investigating the reasons for the disparity in workloads and the viability of redistributing computing resources. All of the complex simulations are run in clouds. The process consisted of two distinct parts. The simulation begins with a randomly generated workload. Second, we combine the workload prediction model with an application and workload-aware scheduling algorithm (AAWAS) [14]. We present a parallel job scheduling approach using computational node workload prediction AAWAS to simplify the AAWAS algorithm. Experimental results reveal that AAWA is superior to other algorithms in terms of minimizing makespan and optimizing resource utilization, and the proposed method is compared to FCFS, SJF, Min-Min, and EDF. To make Task scheduling in compute clouds faces various challenges due to the highly dynamic environment, such as availability, access policies, security, and reliability of computing resources. Furthermore, the collaborative nature of cloud computing projects on the internet adds complexity to task scheduling. From simulation results, it is evident that our proposed scheduler AAWAS outperforms A2C, DQN, and PPO across the board by 4.1%, 2.6%, and 3.4%, respectively. Because AAWS relies on policy for learning rather than Q-value, its superiority can be defended. Several environmental factors affect AAWAS and contribute to its consistent learning process and the high chance of accurate predictions. As a result, AAWASC may learn from experiences independently of target networks, and this helps to better generalize the network.

articleTitle: The Internet of Things and Its Impact on EV Charging Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: In order to meet the goals of net-zero emissions and global decarbonization, there is a pressing need for a shift towards greener energy sources as a worldwide phenomenon. The worldwide mobility industry, which relies heavily on fossil fuels, is an ideal target for such efforts as it is accountable for 37% of the most current greenhouse gas emissions. Because of this, the adoption of battery-powered vehicles has speed up on a global scale, which is great news for the environment and efficiency in transportation. In spite of this expansion, there are still significant restrictions in electric vehicle charging infrastructure among buyers of electric vehicles. The resolution of this barrier necessitates the use of methodical measures in order to guarantee smooth operation and integration with the current transportation networks. This research reviews the existing literature to get a better understanding of the interrelationship between the Internet of Things (IoT) and the issues that are associated with electric vehicle (EV) public charging. Additionally, the study highlights the influence that the IoT has on the user experience. The research shows that the Internet of Things IoT may be a strong tool for improving public policy, but its innovative nature faces developmental challenges due to existing government regulations, which might put off potential investors. Therefore, lawmakers should think about reviewing existing regulations to see if they are appropriate for electric vehicle and Internet of Things acceptance, so they don’t act as unintentional roadblocks.

articleTitle: Deep CNN and Machine Learning Methods For Breast Cancer classification: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Breast cancer is still a major global health concern, underscoring the critical need for precise and effective diagnostic techniques. This thorough review paper explores recent developments in breast cancer detection methodologies, with a particular emphasis on the use of transfer learning in conjunction with convolutional neural networks (CNNs), spiking neural networks (SNNs), and conventional machine learning algorithms. We also analyse a variety of approaches and methodologies utilized in recent research endeavours aimed at improving breast cancer detection. Using a variety of imaging modalities such as MRI, mammography, ultrasound, and histology images, we examine how well these approaches can improve the precision and effectiveness of diagnosis. We demonstrate, via painstaking analysis, that transfer learning is a key strategy for utilizing prior knowledge from various domains to enhance model performance in breast cancer diagnosis. Furthermore, we investigate alternative approaches like novel CNN architectures and hierarchical ML-based classification, offering insights into their contributions to the field. The importance of using transfer learning and other cutting-edge methods in breast cancer detection research is highlighted by our review, which ultimately aims to improve patient outcomes and diagnostic accuracy.

articleTitle: Analysis of SDLC Models with Web Engineering Principles
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: The dynamism of web technologies and the emergence of advanced and intricate web applications strongly call for the definition of the software development life cycle paradigms from the perspective of web engineering discipline. Hybrid models like Waterfall, V-Model and Iterative Development have been in use for formal software development while recent development methodologies are Agile. Yet, these models need to be assessed and adapted for the web engineering contexts to fit problems that are specific to web application development, for example, rapid development cycles, high user interaction, the need for scalability and constantly shifting security requirements. This paper, introduces five fundamental SDLC models of web engineering, namely the Waterfall model, V-Model, Spiral model, Agile, and DevOps. It also discusses how developments on basic web engineering components such as client-server model, crossplatform Web, rapid prototyping, and continuous deployment map to various phases of the Web SDLC namely requirement analysis, design, construction, testing, and maintenance. Upon reviewing the strengths and weaknesses of each model as applied to web development, this paper introduces a new approach that combines the best elements of Agility and conventional models into a single framework competent for modern web applications. Hence, the paper endeavors to understand how Web Engineering can improve on traditional SDLC models with the ultimate vision of presenting an optimal paradigm for web application development.Another key theme of this paper is the need to adapt SDLC models to meet the need of Web applications that require integration, flexibility, and usability. Web applications meet complex and dynamic requirements; therefore, web engineering principles have to be created as scalable, secure, and dynamically adaptive to multi-plenary devices and platforms, which mandate iterative and adaptive life cycles. Having evaluated how SDLC models address these requirements, the paper establishes that traditional models are in some ways deficient and proposes enhancements that helpful for web-based projects. It also discuss how current trends such as DevOps and Agile hybrids can be used to deal with issues of speedy deployment and real time feedback to enhance web application reliability, expandability and usability in current complex environment. Web engineering principles’ incorporation into the SDLC methodologies gives the developers a guideline to use in managing the complicated web application developments’ issues without compromising on quality or performance issues.

articleTitle: IoT Based Battery Management System for Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: This paper demonstrates an IoT based Battery Management System (BMS) designed for hybrid charging applications, combining solar and AC power sources to boost energy optimization and consistency. It also monitors the various parameters of battery like Charging status, Battery Health. The system harnesses solar energy through photovoltaic (PV) panels during daylight hours and switches to an AC/DC converter for charging during periods of insufficient sunlight. Key features include intelligent power source selection, efficient energy conversion, and advanced battery monitoring to ensure optimal charging and longevity. The BMS employs real-time data analytics and adaptive algorithms to manage the charging and discharging cycles, maintaining battery health, and maximizes energy utilization. This dual-source approach not only reduces dependence on the grid but also supports sustainable energy practices, making it ideal for residential, commercial, and industrial applications. Experimental results demonstrate the system’s effectiveness in maintaining consistent battery performance and extending operational life under varying environmental conditions.

articleTitle: Energy Management Systems In Hybrid Renewable Energy Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: The rapid growth of electric power has led to an increase in the generation and integration of renewable energy into grids. Integration can affect the security and stability of power systems due to their complexity. An optimal control approach is needed to ensure efficiency, reliability and quality. The employment of Hybrid Renewable Energy Systems (HRES) may address this dilemma by integrating diverse renewable energy sources within a singular framework to enhance mutual support. Incorporating high renewable energy sources aids in stabilizing the supply and demand of energy while also slowly mitigating the downsides of energy generation; nevertheless, combining various energy sources with energy storage systems (ESS) adds complexity to energy administration. This work explores various architectures of hybrid sources like solar wind hydro. The evaluation examines how energy management systems can enhance stability, reliability, and resilience of HRES, while also reducing operational cost and achieving economic goals.

articleTitle: Optimized Baffle Design for Augmented Thermal Transfer in Solar Air Collectors
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Advancements and Key Challenges in Green Energy and Computing (AKGEC)
abstract: Solar air collectors (SACs) in solar air heating systems used for crop drying, space heating, and ventilation experience mitigated heat transfer because of viscous sublayers, low air density and low air thermal capacity. Angled baffles with perforations on heat transfer surfaces improve SAC thermal performance. This paper experimentally analyzes the effect of staggered racetrack-shaped perforated V-baffles at attack angles ($\alpha$) of $45^{\circ}, 60^{\circ}, 120^{\circ}$, and 135°, and pitch ratios ($p / e$) of 2, 6, and 10, with turbulent Reynolds numbers ($R e$) ranging from 5400 to 14,400 in an air heater duct. Results show higher j (Colburn j-factor) and $\boldsymbol{f}$ (Fanning friction factor) for baffled surfaces compared to the plain surface, which decreases with increasing $R e$ and $p / e$. An $\alpha$ of 120° gives the maximum $f / f_{s}$ of 17.99 for $p / e$ of 2 at the highest $R e$, while $\alpha$ of 135° with the same $\mathrm{p} / \mathrm{e}$ yields the maximum j value of 0.00893 at $R e 10,351$. The maximum $j / j_{s}$ and $J F$ factor values are 2.51 and 1.057, respectively, at the highest $R e$. The correlations formulated for j and f align well with the test data.
